[h2] Save Your Lover Before the World is Cursed... [/h2]
Before going into this game, I expected it to be like every other hidden object puzzle game I’ve played. I was very wrong. This game was very different from any other, and honestly, I loved that it was.

In [i]Cursed[/i], our fiance, Albert, receives a mysterious letter about a gratifying job. The only problem is that it’s far away, so he leaves us. Time passed, and we hadn’t received any word from him, causing us to worry. This leads us on a long journey to search for our lover, which is full of many dangers and obstacles. Ghosts, demons, monsters, oh my! Can the main character make it through all the twists and turns and find her lover? Can we prevent the world from turning into hell?

This game is a hidden object puzzle game, but unlike many others, you have a list of objects you must find in a scene. You still need to locate objects, but you just pick them up in locations. However, despite how different this game was, I still had a lot of fun playing through. What I especially loved about this game was the graphics and animations. Each location was beautiful, and I adored how everything looked. The animations for objects, creatures, and so on were in 3D, which I found really cool. What’s more, the designs for the monsters and other creatures were impressive.

While the story may not be the greatest, it all made sense and was enjoyable. There’s a lot to admire with this game, so I’m pleased I checked it out!

[h2]Cursed - Ein spannendes Wimmelbildspiel, das Rätselliebhaber begeistert. Keine Spoiler.[/h2]

[Quote]"Cursed" ist ein Wimmelbildspiel, das sich in die lange Tradition von Spielen dieses Genres einreiht. Als Fan von Rätselspielen habe ich "Cursed" ausprobiert und wurde angenehm überrascht von der Qualität des Spielerlebnisses.[/quote]

Das Spiel "Cursed" präsentiert eine fesselnde Handlung, die den Spieler in eine mysteriöse und düstere Welt entführt. Die Geschichte dreht sich um ein verzaubertes Schloss, das von einem Fluch heimgesucht wird. Als Spieler schlüpft man in die Rolle eines Ermittlers, der beauftragt wurde, das Geheimnis des Schlosses zu lüften und den Fluch zu brechen. Die Erzählung ist gut geschrieben und sorgt für Spannung und Neugierde, während man immer tiefer in die düstere Geschichte eintaucht.

Die Spielwelt von "Cursed" ist detailliert gestaltet und bietet eine Vielzahl von Schauplätzen, die erkundet werden müssen. Die Wimmelbildszenen sind liebevoll gestaltet und bieten zahlreiche versteckte Objekte, die gefunden werden müssen. Die Umgebungen sind atmosphärisch und tragen zur Gesamtstimmung des Spiels bei.

Die Rätsel und Minispiele in "Cursed" sind abwechslungsreich und herausfordernd. Sie erfordern oft logisches Denken und Kombinationsfähigkeiten, was das Spiel besonders für Rätselliebhaber attraktiv macht. Die Schwierigkeit der Rätsel steigt im Verlauf des Spiels an, was für eine angemessene Herausforderung sorgt.

Die Grafiken und die Soundkulisse von "Cursed" sind ansprechend. Die Hintergrundmusik und die Soundeffekte tragen zur Atmosphäre des Spiels bei und verstärken die Spannung.

Insgesamt ist "Cursed" ein gelungenes Wimmelbildspiel, das Rätselliebhaber ansprechen wird. Die spannende Handlung, die liebevoll gestalteten Szenen und die anspruchsvollen Rätsel machen es zu einer unterhaltsamen Erfahrung. Wenn Sie gerne nach versteckten Objekten suchen und sich gerne kniffligen Rätseln stellen, sollten Sie "Cursed" definitiv ausprobieren. Es bietet stundenlangen Spielspaß und ein fesselndes Abenteuer in einer mysteriösen Welt.

6/10 Cursed is a beautiful gothic style horror adventure puzzle hidden object game where you play as a woman who goes through a lot to find her husband.

My takeaway: The art is to die for, for the people who enjoy the gothic aesthetic. The music really captures the moments you’re in and the characters feel believable. As far as the story goes- this one is pretty out there. You play the heroine as she tries to find her husband after he goes missing from a business endeavor and you end up going on a wild goose chase to find out what happened. A lot of the game is voiced and is pretty easy to follow despite the story being a bit complicated. None of it was predictable and although I hadn’t played the game in quite some time I very vividly remember this one- which is a pretty great achievement. The achievements for this title are easy to get and are story and gameplay centered. It should take you around 5 hours to complete.

The hidden object puzzle aspect in Cursed is exactly how hidden puzzle games SHOULD be and if you’re a fan of that type of gameplay I highly recommend trying this out. Especially when it’s on sale.

   [*] Very entertaining and easy to play.

   [*] Story is original and enticing.

   [*] Voice acting is wonderful!
   [*] No glitches or bugs and plays smoothly.
   [*] 100% worth it during sale.
[/list]

[u]Cons[/u]
[list]

This isn't a hidden object game, no matter what the tags say. It's a point and click adventure. And not a great one at that. Most games, HOG or adventure, at least try and nudge you in the right direction. This game does that, but seemingly at random and only for the most obvious items. "Hmm, this reminds me of something." Sure it does, you saw the lock one screen ago and here's the shaped key.

When it comes to puzzles, it feels like three different teams designed this game. Some puzzles have hints, some don't. Some are skippable, some aren't. As to why they are there? I don't know because they shouldn't be, no one in this game has a valid reason to stop you. If anything the main bad guy should be helping you and there's a distinctly odd moment where he seems to have realized a plan where you were hindered, or Gods forbid, killed, would have undone everything. 

Gameplay consists main of fetch quests with shaped keys or items hidden in plain sight. Sometimes right in the same area they are needed in.  The biggest challenge was that the game was often silent and would not give a single clue of what to do on a puzzle or with an object. Overall, it was pretty in a dated way, but the uncanny valley characters will forever haunt my dreams. 

I got it at half price on the winter sale and honestly can't recommend it even at that price.

[b]Cursed[/b] is a horror-themed point & click game, where you play as a lady in a daunting task to search for her fiance in a mansion filled with a variety of demons and vile creatures

[h1]STORY[/h1]
The story is told from the first perspective, while you explore into the deep of the mansion, you encounter some NPC and letters left by Albert (the fiance) to tell you what is going on. 

The storyline itself is pretty straight forward. It starts with a letter Albert left to you with an address to it. You arrived at the mansion that looks like no one lives there for a long time, but there's a lot of unnatural phenomena that are trying to stop you to advance further, while sometimes the NPC you encounter will tell you what you must do to find your fiance. 

[h1]GAMEPLAY[/h1]
Cursed gameplay is like any other point & click game that featured : 
[list]
[*]Inventory, where you stored items you found and combine.
[*]Map, to easily navigate to the area you have visited. 
[*]Navigation help, to highlight point of interest in the area.
[*]Hint, to give you tips on what to do next. The hint is limited and refreshed by time.
[/list]

While there is no difficulty level, the puzzle it present is quite easy, as any key you find is very distinctive to which things you unlock. It took me around 2 hours to finish it. 

[h1]VISUAL[/h1]
Visual art is nicely done and smooth, with some cutscene and interaction on the object being animated. The object of interest is blended closely with its environment, which makes it not too easy to find. 

[h1]AUDIO[/h1]
[list]
[*]The music is lowkey fitting the horror/thrill ambience. 
[*]Full voice acting, though it's just ordinary and not memorable. 
[*]Sound effect on object interaction is good. And the sound while on cutscene is spot on to make jumpscare.  
[/list]

This was one of the first Hidden Object games I had ever played and it's definitely a great game to play.  To me, this seems like a Victorian-era setting with, of course, fantasy elements, though I think this was done very well.

The story is very linear, and it makes a lot of sense from start to finish.  There are the notes from your fiance that keep you grounded in the events going on from his perspective, and he keeps reiterating how much he loves you and wants your input.  It's very clear that someone was purposefully trying to keep his notes from you, in the beginning it seemed malicious but you come to find out it was for your own safety.  The monsters in it were definitely unique and horrifying.  The goblin in the tree and in the cage were definitely the most frightening creatures, and the Demon definitely shared a lot of features with them to help immerse the player in the idea that hell and the real world were combining.  The man that essentially started it all wasn't really an evil man either.  He was just a heartbroken man that couldn't accept your death and was willing to do anything to get you back.  There are some points where the characters aren't redeemable, but in this case, he realized that you weren't safe and what he had done was wrong, and I honestly was very happy that everyone got a happy ending in the end.

Overall a very good game, even though I would have liked maybe a bit more descriptions on everything to try and help figure out what I needed to do.  Would absolutely recommend playing it.

Cursed is part of a large stable of 'hidden object' puzzle genre games, the kind that feel like a cheap mobile point and are more 'click around the screen' than 'puzzle'. 

Cursed ends pretty fun to play as long as you accept it for what it is. The plot is dumb but spooky in a carnival-ride kind of way, and the little cutscenes are poorly animated and cheaply made, with cringy, wooden dialogue- but the effect is charming rather than annoying. The only bad part is there is a few puzzles where the hitbox to click on something is severely messed up(specifically, there's a part where you need to loosen four screws, and the places to click them are horribly off-center).

Cursed is the equivalent of a cheap B-movie. It's easy, cheap(though you might want to wait for a sale), we all know why you're watching, and it's a fun way to burn two hours.
